items.title: Scott Yanow interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 22, 2021
items.q: When it doubt I’ll put on Eddie Condon. The thing is sometimes people get depressed and I say, “Well, put on Dixieland, the world’s happiest music, you’ll be happy.”

ctx.x: What’s on your to-do list at the moment?

I don’t know. I don’t know what I’m doing. I’ve been listening to a lot of re-issues but I mean recently I listened to some Stan Kenton ballad albums because I reviewed it for something, for one magazine. And then a George Duke album that actually has him playing jazz in the early 70s. But as far as new music goes, I don’t know there’s an Anat Cohen record, a Brazilian album, and I’m looking forward to getting the John Coltrane “A Love Supreme” the live version that just came out. But it’s on a moment’s notice.…
Yes and I want to take note that you mentioned John Coltrane followed by the phrase, “A Moment’s Notice.” Well done, even if it was an improvisation.
